title: Generative Video at the Speed of Light — Keegan McCallum, uRun
talk_summary: A founder pitch for uRun, an inference provider for real-time generative video, showing efficiency gains in video models (distills, long-horizon generation) and demoing a React component plus Python runtime for streaming multi-model pipelines.

takeaways.technique: Distilled small model as cheap default
takeaways.what_they_do: They serve Helios, a distilled 14B video model, as a cheap fast tier that matches last year's frontier quality at a fraction of cost, reserving frontier models for higher-fidelity renders.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Helios is a distill of Juan 2.1 14B
takeaways.numbers: claims ~1/100th the cost vs a minutes-long frontier generation; $10 ≈ 3 hours of continuous generated video

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe wiring multiple models into continuous streaming workflows with a programmable Python runtime that generates asynchronously, so stages overlap instead of running sequentially.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're going to want a model wire multiple models together in continuous streaming workflows

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose their platform via a CLI and an MCP server so agents can build applications against it programmatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've actually built one that will let folks hook into a CLI or an MCP server
